# homebuycheck.com
> Free home affordability calculator. Find out how much house you can afford from your income, debts and down payment, using the 28/36 rule.

## What this tool does
- Calculates the maximum home price at which housing costs stay under 28% of gross monthly income and total debt payments stay under 36%
- Models principal and interest, state property tax, homeowner's insurance (0.5% of the home price a year) and PMI (0.5% of the loan a year when the down payment is under 20%)
- Covers all 50 states plus DC
- Inputs: gross annual income, monthly debts, down payment, interest rate, a 15 or 30 year term, and state

## How it works
The 28/36 rule is the standard used by most conventional mortgage lenders. The calculator finds the lower of:
1. The maximum home price where the full housing payment (principal, interest, property tax, insurance, PMI) stays under 28% of gross monthly income
2. The maximum home price where that payment plus existing monthly debts stays under 36% of gross monthly income

## Data sources
- State property tax: Tax Foundation, "Property Taxes by State and County, 2026" (2024 American Community Survey 5-year estimates), applied as each state's effective rate
- City pages: Zillow Home Value Index for median home prices and HUD FY2026 Section 8 Income Limits for median household income
- The interest rate and down payment are your inputs. Insurance and PMI are the calculator's own assumptions, not quotes

## Key facts (computed by this calculator at a 7% rate, 30 year term, no other debts)
- A $500,000 home with 20% down needs about $128,000 to $156,000 of annual income, depending on the state's property tax
- With 5% down the same home needs about $158,000 to $186,000, because PMI is added
- When the 36% limit is the one that binds, each extra $1,000 a month of debt payments lowers the maximum price by about $116,000 to $125,000
- On a $400,000 home, 20% down instead of 5% to 10% removes about $150 to $160 a month of PMI

## Page types
- City pages: https://homebuycheck.com/city/{slug} (181 metros; example /city/houston)
- Income pages: https://homebuycheck.com/salary/{income} (10 incomes from $50,000 to $300,000; example /salary/100000). These assume no other debts, a 30 year mortgage and the Texas average property tax rate
- Methodology: https://homebuycheck.com/methodology

## Not supported
The calculator does not accept URL parameters. Link to the city or income page you mean.

## Tool URL
https://homebuycheck.com
